title: Tell a dispatched worker where its worktree is and where the store lives
action: dispatch prepare --claim already claims the cell and reserves every cell.files entry under the worker nickname (prepare.rs:782-885) and already inlines the cell JSON into the worker-cell template (prepare.rs:398-426), but neither the envelope nor the template ever names the worktree. A worker dispatched into a granted feature worktree therefore does not know where to work, and does not know its cell and claim live in another checkout - one reported having to read the claim across checkouts by hand. Add it: when find_granted_worktree_for_feature (status_full/topology.rs:198-216) resolves a granted worktree for the cell's feature, the prepare envelope carries worktree_root and control_root, and the worker-cell template gains a Location block naming both - work here, the store is there. When there is no granted worktree the payload and the rendered prompt stay byte-identical to today. The template is include_str! compiled with a disk-vs-embedded byte-match guard (prompt.rs:33,72-89), so packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md and .bee/bin/prompts/worker-cell.md must both change and stay identical, and the release manifest must be regenerated.
verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml verbs::drivers && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

truths: the envelope names worktree_root and control_root for a feature with a granted worktree
the rendered prompt tells the worker where to work and that the store is elsewhere
a feature with no worktree renders byte-identically to today
both prompt copies stay byte-identical and the embedded guard passes

trace.outcome: granted-worktree location envelope + prompt block, byte-identical without a grant
